modules.name: ShortenService
modules.responsibility: Generate and persist short codes for long URLs, enforce idempotency for repeat submissions, and validate/normalize input URLs.

modules.name: RedirectService
modules.responsibility: Resolve a short code to its target URL and issue an HTTP redirect, emitting a click event as a side effect without blocking the redirect.
interfaces:
class Redirector(Protocol):
    def redirect(self, code: str, ctx: RequestContext) -> RedirectResult: ...

modules.name: StatsService
modules.responsibility: Record click events and aggregate per-link click statistics (totals, time buckets, referrer/UA breakdowns).
injection_points: Clock (for deterministic time bucketing in tests)

modules.name: RateLimiter
modules.responsibility: Enforce per-client request quotas on shorten and redirect endpoints using a configurable window/algorithm.
interfaces:
class RateLimiter(Protocol):
    def check(self, key: str, action: str) -> RateDecision: ...

modules.name: Persistence
modules.responsibility: Provide storage abstractions (LinkStore, ClickStore, RateStore) decoupling business logic from the concrete database, enabling swap between in-memory, SQLite, and Redis.
interfaces:
class LinkStore(Protocol):
    def save(self, link: ShortLink) -> None: ...
    def get(self, code: str) -> ShortLink | None: ...
    def get_by_url(self, long_url: str) -> ShortLink | None: ...
injection_points: Concrete backend selected via factory/config at composition root

ux_flows.name: Shorten a URL
steps: Client POSTs {long_url} (optionally custom_alias) to /shorten with API key
Existing link reused if same long_url, else CodeGenerator mints code
ux_flows.success_criteria: Valid URL returns a working short_url in a single request

ux_flows.name: Follow a short link
ux_flows.success_criteria: Known active code redirects in <50ms p95 without waiting on stats write

ux_flows.name: View click stats
ux_flows.success_criteria: Owner sees totals and daily breakdown in one call

customer_journey: A developer integrating link shortening obtains an API key, calls POST /api/shorten with a long URL, and immediately receives a compact short_url. They embed it in emails or messages. Recipients click the short link and are redirected near-instantly to the destination; each click is recorded out-of-band so redirect latency stays low. Later, the developer queries /api/stats/{code} (or the CLI) to see total clicks, unique-visitor estimates, daily trends, and top referrers — all scoped to links they own. Abusive or runaway clients are transparently throttled with 429 + Retry-After, protecting service health without manual intervention.

experience_metric.name: shorten_round_trip
experience_metric.target: Shorten a URL in 1 API call (or 1 CLI command) and redirect p95 < 50ms
experience_metric.measurement: API integration test asserts single-request shorten; load test measures redirect latency excluding stats write

architecture_decisions.title: Decouple click recording from the redirect hot path
architecture_decisions.context: Redirect latency is the primary user-facing performance metric, but every redirect must also produce a click event for stats. Synchronously writing the event on the redirect path couples redirect availability/latency to the stats store and risks slowing or failing redirects when the stats backend is degraded.
architecture_decisions.decision: RedirectService depends on a ClickRecorder Protocol and emits events fire-and-forget (buffered/async). The redirect returns as soon as the link is resolved; click persistence happens off the critical path. ClickStore is a separate injected backend from LinkStore.
architecture_decisions.rationale: Separation of concerns and dependency inversion: redirect correctness depends only on LinkStore, not on stats durability. Allows independent scaling and backend choice for write-heavy click data, and keeps p95 redirect latency low. Friction signal: synchronous coupling would surface as hard-to-test redirect logic entangled with stats mocks.
consequences: Click counts are eventually consistent and may drop events on crash unless a durable queue is added
Redirect and stats backends can scale/fail independently
Tests for RedirectService mock only ClickRecorder, not a full stats DB
Need a buffer/flush policy and at-least-once option for stronger guarantees

architecture_decisions.title: Storage behind Protocol stores with pluggable backends
architecture_decisions.context: The project must run as a lightweight CLI/dev tool (in-memory/SQLite) and as a scalable service (Redis/Postgres) without rewriting business logic.
architecture_decisions.decision: Define LinkStore, ClickStore, RateStore Protocols; select concrete implementations at a composition root via config/factory.
architecture_decisions.rationale: Dependency inversion keeps modules testable with in-memory fakes and lets deployment choose the backend.
consequences: Backend swaps require no business-logic changes

threat_model.description: Open redirect / phishing: attacker shortens a malicious URL to leverage the service's trusted domain, or enumerates codes to harvest destinations.
threat_model.mitigation: URL validation + denylist/scheme allowlist (http/https only), optional safe-browsing check, random non-sequential codes to resist enumeration.

threat_model.description: Flood of shorten or redirect requests exhausts storage or compute.
threat_model.mitigation: Per-API-key and per-IP token-bucket rate limiting on both endpoints with 429 + Retry-After; quotas configurable.

threat_model.description: Click logs containing raw client IPs constitute PII that could deanonymize users if leaked.
threat_model.mitigation: Store only salted SHA-256 IP hashes and coarsened UA/geo; never persist raw IP; enforce retention TTL and owner-scoped stats access.

threat_model.description: A client views or alters stats/links it does not own.
threat_model.mitigation: API-key authentication and ownership checks (creator_hash) on stats and management endpoints.

privacy_inventory.retention: Raw IP not stored; salted hash retained 90 days
privacy_inventory.encryption: SHA-256 with rotating salt at rest; TLS in transit
privacy_inventory.erasure_path: Hash auto-expires via TTL; owner link deletion purges associated ClickEvents
Purged on link deletion or TTL
Purged on link deletion or TTL

i18n_plan.framework: gettext-style message catalogs for CLI/API error messages
i18n_plan.rtl_strategy: CLI output is locale-formatted text; RTL (ar) handled by terminal/bidi; no UI layout mirroring needed for API. IDN hosts normalized via punycode on ingest.
i18n_plan.date_handling: Stats timestamps stored UTC ISO-8601; rendered in caller locale at the edge

open_questions: Should short codes be reused/idempotent per long_url globally or per API key (affects privacy leakage across tenants)?
Required durability for click events — is best-effort acceptable or do we need an at-least-once durable queue (impacts ADR-001)?
Are custom aliases supported in v1, and what is the namespace/collision policy?
What is the default link expiration policy, if any?
Is geo-IP lookup in scope (adds a PII-processing dependency)?

sections.title: Module Boundaries
sections.content: Five modules: ShortenService, RedirectService, StatsService, RateLimiter, Persistence. Each business module depends on Protocol stores injected at a composition root.

sections.title: Data Model
sections.content: ShortLink (code PK, long_url, creator_hash), ClickEvent (ip_hash only, no raw IP), ClickStats aggregation view, RateDecision. PII minimized via hashing and coarsening.

sections.title: Key Decisions
sections.content: ADR-001 decouples click recording from the redirect hot path (async fire-and-forget) for low latency and testability. ADR-002 puts storage behind pluggable Protocol backends.

sections.title: Threat & Privacy
sections.content: Top threats: open-redirect/enumeration, DoS, PII leakage from click logs. Mitigations: URL allowlist + random codes, token-bucket rate limiting, IP hashing + retention TTL + owner-scoped access.

sections.title: Digest
sections.content: url-shortener v3: 5 modules (Shorten, Redirect, Stats, RateLimiter, Persistence) over injected Protocol stores. Data: ShortLink + ClickEvent (hashed IP, no raw PII) + aggregated ClickStats. Flows: shorten (1 call), redirect (p95<50ms, async click record), owner-scoped stats. Metric: shorten in 1 command/call. ADR-001: decouple click recording from redirect hot path; ADR-002: pluggable storage backends. STRIDE top-3: open-redirect/enumeration (allowlist+random codes), DoS (token-bucket rate limit, 429+Retry-After), click-log PII leak (salted IP hash, 90d TTL, owner-scoped). Open Qs: idempotency scope, click durability guarantee, custom aliases, expiration, geo-IP scope.
